title: Helsefagarbeider 60% på Gauselskogen
description:
Har du interesse for eller erfaring med å jobbe som helsefagarbeider i døgntilbud innen tverrfaglig spesialisert rusbehandling (TSB), så kan dette være jobben for deg. Vi har ledig 60 % stilling som helsefagarbeider på Gauselskogen behandlingsenter i avdeling for rus og avhengighetsbehandling (ARA).Gauselskogen gir tilbud om døgnbehandling til voksne med vedvarende alvorlig rus og avhengighetsvansker gjerne i kombinasjon med psykisk lidelse og somatiske skadevirkninger. Enheten har 12 behandlingsplasser.

Gauselskogen er tverrfaglig sammensatt av medisinskfaglig, sosialfaglig og psykologfaglig kompetanse. Vi fokuserer på samhandling med øvrige tjenestetilbud og nettverk for å sikre et helhetlig behandlingstilbud. Som tverrfaglig spesialisert rusbehandling ønsker vi å gi pasientene våre et helhetlig, individuelt og integrert behandlingstilbud, i tråd med avdelingens visjon og mål. Hos oss vil du få anledning til å jobbe innenfor et spennende fagfelt med varierte problemstillinger og møte mennesker med ulik bakgrunn og utfordringer. Stillingen er forankret i enhetens behandlingsavdeling.

Vi har følgende målsettinger: 

  • Tilstrebe rusfrihet
  • Fremme fysisk og psykisk helse
  • Styrke relasjoner og nettverk
  • Styrke sosiale og praktiske forhold og ferdigheter
  • Fremme kunnskap og opplevelse av kultur og kreativitet

Årsplan med arbeid hver tredje helg, ikke arbeid på natt.

Attester, vitnemål og eventuell annen relevant dokumentasjon må vedlegges søknaden. 

Arbeidsoppgaver
  • Pasientoppfølging i behandlingsavdelingen med fokus på observasjon, kartlegging og behandling
  • Dokumentasjon av pasientene sine behov samt iverksettelse av miljøterapeutiske tiltak
  • Følge opp somatiske problemstillinger i henhold til pakkeforløp til psykisk helse og rus 
  • Bidra til faglig utvikling av sengeposten
  • Sikre god faglig kvalitet på behandlingen
  • Deltagelse i teamarbeid rundt enkeltpasienter
  • Ivareta pasienter med abstinensproblematikk
  • Yte faglig god behandling for pasienter med rusmiddelavhengighet
  • Tilrettelegge for at brukermedvirkning og involvering i egen behandlingsprosess blir ivaretatt
  • Være medansvarlig for et godt arbeidsmiljø
Kvalifikasjoner

  • Relevant erfaring/kompetanse innen døgndrift rusbehandling og/eller psykisk helsearbeid vektlegges

Søkere som har annet morsmål enn norsk, svensk eller dansk, og som ikke har fullført norskspråklig videregående skole, må minimum ha bestått norsktest på B2 nivå. Dokumentasjon må vedlegges søknaden. Ved ansettelse av allerede fast ansatt i foretaket kan en unntaksvis, i særlige tilfeller, fravike kravet om bestått norsktest på B2-nivå
Personlige egenskaper
  • Personlig egnethet vektlegges særlig og engasjement for brukergruppen er en forutsetning
  • Du må ha gode kommunikasjons- og samarbeidsevner
  • Du må ha evne til å arbeide selvstendig så vel som i team
  • Du må ha en løsningsorientert og fleksibel tilnærming til arbeidets utfordringer
  • Være tilpasningsdyktig og takle høyt tempo med ro og faglig holdning
  • Bidra til et godt arbeidsmiljø
  • Menn oppfordres til å søke på grunn av personalgruppens sammensetning
Vi tilbyr

title: Avdelingsleder til avdeling Håpet.
description:
Avdeling Håpet er en avdeling i stadig utvikling som pr i dag gir tjenester til brukere som bor i egne hjem i området Mortensnes, Håpet, Bo i nord og Workinnmarka. Våre kontorer er lokalisert ved Mortensnes omsorgssenter.   Avdelingen arbeider med hensiktsmessig fordeling av oppgaver for å sikre riktig kompetanse på riktig sted, også med tanke på kvalitetssikring av tjenesten.

Vi benytter kalenderplan for langsiktig planlegging og forutsigbarhet. Vi er fremtidsrettet med bruk av den nyeste teknologi for tjenesten. Avdelingen har god fagdekning, sykepleiere jobber i eget sykepleierteam på tvers av to avdelinger. Vi samarbeider godt tverrfaglig, både innad, og på tvers av, avdelinger.

På enheten har vi egen farmasøyt, ernæringsfysiolog og "Mestring-i-hjemmet"-team med ergo- og fysioterapeuter. Tromsø kommune har høyt fokus på egenmestring i brukers hjem.

Vi søker en stabil, trygg og utviklingsorientert avdelingsleder. Den vi søker må være oppriktig interessert i faget. Du må kunne se nytte og verdien i alle dine ansatte, i alle ledd. Avdelingsleder må ha evne til å motivere og legge til rette for tett samarbeid blant egne ansatte og på tvers av avdelingene. En arbeidshverdag hos oss krever at du er motivert, strukturert og kan jobbe med både kort- og langsiktige mål knyttet opp mot virksomhetsplanen.

Leders støtteapparat i administrasjon består av erfarne og dyktige medarbeidere som fag- og kvalitetskoordinator, ressursbase, administrasjonskonsulent og personalkonsulent i tillegg til øvrige avdelingsledere og enhetsleder.

Arbeidsoppgaver
  • Overordnet faglig ansvar for avdelingen.
  • Daglig drift. Det er forventet økning i brukergrunnlaget, og leder må være med i planlegging for å møte økt behov.
  • Kontakt med brukere, pårørende, lege, sykehus og interne samarbeidspartnere.
  • Personalansvar.
  • Økonomiansvar.
  • Ansvar for kvalitet og HMS.
    Kvalifikasjoner
    • Norsk autorisasjon som sykepleier.
    • Erfaring fra arbeid med målgruppen ønskes.
    • God norsk muntlig og skriftlig framstillingsevne.
    • Lederutdanning og/eller relevant ledererfaring. Søkere uten lederutdanning, må påregne å begynne slik utdanning innen to år.  
    Personlige egenskaper

     

    • Se sine medarbeidere og verdien av deres kompetanse.
    • Du er tydelig og trygg i lederrollen, besluttsom og tillitsvekkende.
    • God på kommunikasjon og relasjonsbygging.
    • Kan jobbe selvstendig og ta raske beslutninger.
    • Er positiv og samarbeidsvillig.
    • Behandler pasienter og medarbeidere med respekt.
    • Er fleksibel, omstillingsdyktig og tro mot beslutninger som blir tatt.
    • Strukturert og nøyaktig.
    • Personlig egnethet vil vektlegges ved ansettelse.
    Vi tilbyr
    • Stillingen er plassert i stillingskode 7451 Leder. Årslønn 730 400 – 867 900 kr. 
    • Selvstendige arbeidsoppgaver med gode, faglige utviklingsmuligheter.
    • Gode pensjons- og forsikringsordninger.
    • Bedriftshelsetjeneste.
    • Tilhørighet i et tverrfaglig og lærerikt miljø.
    • Velferdsordninger.

    Annet

    • Tilsetting skjer i henhold til gjeldende lover, reglementer og tariffavtaler.
    • Vi gjør oppmerksom på at søkere kan føres opp på offentlig søkerliste selv om søkeren har bedt om anonymitet. Dette blir du i så fall varslet om.
    • Ved tilsetting må gyldig politiattest iht. helse- og omsorgstjenesteloven §5-4 fremlegges.
    • Ved tilsetting kreves tuberkuloseundersøkelse for søkere som i løpet av de siste tre årene har oppholdt seg sammenhengende mer enn tre måneder i land med høy forekomst av tuberkulose iht. tuberkuloseforskriftens § 3.1 og 3.2.
    • Attester og vitnemål legges ved søknad før intervju.
    • Referanser registreres på forespørsel etter intervju.
    • Søknad sendes elektronisk via Webcruiter.

     

    KontaktinformasjonRonny Mentzoni, enhetsleder, 90 77 71 34 ArbeidsstedØrnevegen 6 9015 TROMSØ Nøkkelinformasjon:Arbeidsgiver: Tromsø kommune Referansenr.: 5205108016 Stillingsprosent: 100% Fast Søknadsfrist: 06.12.2026

    Om arbeidsgiveren:

    Tromsø kommune er Nord-Norges største kommune med omtrent 79 900 innbyggere. Den ligger i naturskjønne omgivelser og har en strategisk plass i nordområdene. Byen har universitet, universitetssykehus, godt flyrutetilbud og et yrende kultur- og idrettsliv. Kommunen har omtrent 7 000 medarbeidere, fordelt på 86 enheter.

    Vi er en stor samfunnsaktør som skal sikre et best mulig tjenestetilbud og service til lokalsamfunnet og kommunens innbyggere. Vi bidrar til utvikling av lokal infrastruktur, næring og kultur. Vi ønsker medarbeidere med ulik bakgrunn, fagkombinasjoner, kompetanse, livserfaring og perspektiver. Det gir oss et mangfoldig arbeidsmiljø som setter oss bedre i stand til å løse oppgavene. Les mer her om jobb i Tromsø kommune.

    Det er viktig for oss å ha en arbeidsstyrke som representerer befolkningen, og vi tilrettelegger arbeidsplassen ved behov. Vi oppfordrer alle som er kvalifisert til å søke, uavhengig av alder, kjønn, funksjonsgrad eller etnisk- og kulturell bakgrunn.

    Nordøya hjemmetjeneste driver hjemmebasert omsorg nord på Tromsøya. Vi har fire avdelinger, fordelt med to utetjenester og to omsorgsboligavdelinger. Vi har egen hjemmehjelpsbase og driver i tillegg nattjeneste for store deler av Tromsø kommune. Våre lokaler ligger i Mortensnes omsorgssenter på Håpet. Følg oss gjerne på Facebook.

title: Researcher in Biometric Security and Anti-Fraud Technologies
description:
This is NTNU

NTNU is a broad-based university with a technical-scientific profile and a focus in professional education. The university is located in three cities with headquarters in Trondheim.

At NTNU, 9,000 employees and 43,000 students work to create knowledge for a better world.

You can find more information about working at NTNU and the application process here.

   

Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WWHqR5i1FHE&feature=youtu.beAbout the Job

The Department of Information Security and Communication Technology (IIK) at NTNU Gjøvik has a vacancy for a Researcher in Socio-Technical Fraud Systems. 

The position is for an intended period of 24 months and is part of SAFE – Secure Anti-Fraud Excellence Center, funded by Sparebankstiftelsen Hedmark and SpareBank 1 Østlandet in collaboration with NTNU and industry partners.The researcher will be a key member of WP1 and lead its socio-technical analysis of financial fraud, hosted at CCIS, NTNU Gjøvik. WP1 examines vishing and safe-account fraud and a proposed extension to investment fraud. It distinguishes technical authentication and payment confirmation from legally valid consent.

The research reconstructs how fraud unfolds across channels, while focusing detection and intervention on evidence actually visible to the bank between customer authentication and payment authorisation. Off-bank calls, screen sharing and remote-access activities are described where case sources support them, but are not assumed to be observable by the bank.

The work draws on public decisions of Finansklagenemnda, court judgments, and anonymised or otherwise lawfully accessible cases from SAFE’s banking partners. Results feed into cognitive experiments (WP2), detection research (WP3), scientific publications and a policy white paper.Center for Cyber and Information Security (CCIS) at NTNU will host the SAFE Project.Your immediate leader is head of department.

Duties of the position
  • Build a systematically coded corpus of fraud cases from public decisions and lawfully accessible bank material, using a shared template and a cross-channel timeline.
  • Develop evidence-based fraud scripts for vishing and safe-account fraud and, subject to scope confirmation, investment fraud, including interim inputs for WP2.
  • Map each fraud stage, the channels involved, signs of real-time guidance, and what is actually observable by the bank between authentication and payment authorisation.
  • Identify legitimate customer activities with similar bank-visible patterns, to support realistic false-alarm testing without using victim characteristics as automatic detection features.
  • Study intervention points and fraudster adaptation, including cases where the bank suspects fraud but the customer rejects warnings; help plan a tabletop session with a banking partner.
  • Analyse legal, ethical and governance conditions for collecting, using and sharing fraud-related signals, including privacy, bank confidentiality and interbank cooperation.
  • Examine the conditions for transaction warnings, delays, refusals and escalation, with attention to customer consent, liability and loss allocation.
  • Assess payee verification and, in investment-fraud cases, checks of providers against Finanstilsynet’s register and market warnings; distinguish these from bank-account verification.
  • Provide fraud scripts and realistic look-alike scenarios to WP2 and observability findings, intervention points and lawful-signal constraints to WP3.
  • Prepare WP1 deliverables, scientific publications and a policy white paper, and present findings to the SAFE Advisory Board and project partners.
  • Contribute, where relevant, to SAFE continuing education (EVU), project reporting and research proposal development.
Required selection criteria
  • A master’s degree (120 ECTS or equivalent) or a PhD in information security, socio-technical systems, criminology, information systems, law and technology, or a closely related field.
  • Documented experience with systematic analysis of qualitative material, such as case files, legal decisions, interviews or incident reports, using a coding scheme or structured method.
  • Knowledge of social engineering and fraud in digital channels, such as vishing, authorised push payment fraud or investment fraud.
  • Understanding of digital banking and payment processes, including authentication, payment initiation and customer interaction channels.
  • Ability to recognise legal, ethical and data-protection questions and work with relevant specialists on their implications for fraud prevention research.
  • Reading comprehension of Norwegian or another Scandinavian language sufficient to analyse Norwegian case material and legal decisions.
  • Good written and spoken English and the ability to prepare clear, well-structured research reports.
Preferred selection criteria
  • A PhD in a relevant field, or research experience after completion of the master’s degree.
  • Experience in applied research projects involving banks, financial crime specialists or regulatory and legal experts.
  • Experience in crime script analysis, situational crime prevention, socio-technical analysis, or process and threat modelling.
  • Knowledge of Norwegian or EU rules on payment services, data protection, bank confidentiality or financial crime prevention.
  • Experience in fraud prevention, anti-money laundering, compliance or incident handling in the financial sector.
  • Experience in planning and facilitating interviews, workshops or tabletop exercises with practitioners.
  • Relevant scientific publications or reports on fraud, cybercrime or socio-technical security.
  • Skills in structuring and analysing data, for example using Python, R or NVivo.
  • Spoken Norwegian or another Scandinavian language for cooperation with partner banks.
Personal characteristics
  • Highly motivated for applied and collaborative research with financial-sector partners.
  • Analytical, structured and precise in the handling of research evidence and sources.
  • Discreet and reliable in handling confidential case material and working across disciplines.
  • Self-driven, communicative and able to deliver to agreed deadlines.
  • Personal suitability will be emphasized.
We offer
  • Exciting and stimulating research tasks in a strong international academic environment
  • Active collaboration with leading industrial and research partners in Norway and abroad.
  • A professional and inclusive work environment.
  • Favorable terms in the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund
  • Employee benefits at NTNU
Salary and conditions

As a researcher (code 1108/1109) you are normally paid from gross NOK 580 000– NOK 750 000 per annum before tax, depending on qualifications and seniority. As required by law, 2% of this salary will be deducted and paid into the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund.

The engagement is to be made in accordance with the regulations in force concerning State Employees and Civil Servants, and the acts relating to Control of the Export of Strategic Goods, Services and Technology. Candidates who by assessment of the application and attachment are seen to conflict with the criteria in the latter law will be prohibited from recruitment to NTNU. 

The intended appointment period is 24 months. Starting date at the latest: 1st April 2027.  Please note that loss of external funding is considered equivalent to loss of work assignments, see §19 (1) of the public Employees act. In the event of dismissal by the employer, the notice period is according to §22 (1) of the Public Employers Act. 

It is a prerequisite that you can be present at and accessible to the institution on a daily basis. After the appointment you must assume that there may be changes in the area of work.

About the application

Your application and supporting documentation must be in English. 

The attachments (including a description of your scientific work) must accompany the application as these documents form the basis of the application assessment. The documents must be in  English. 

Please note: the application will only be assessed on the basis of the information we have received by the application deadline. Therefore, make sure that your application clearly shows how your skills and experience meet the criteria described above. The application and all attachments must be sent electronically via Jobbnorge.no. If you are invited to an interview, you must bring certified copies of certificates and diplomas upon request.

If, for any reason, you have taken a career break or have had an atypical career and wish to disclose this in your application, the selection committee will take this into account, recognizing that the quantity of your research may be reduced as a result.

Your application must include:

  • Motivation letter describing your interest in SAFE and socio-technical research on financial fraud (maximum one page).
  • CV and relevant certificates.
  • Transcripts, diplomas and diploma supplements for completed degrees (BSc, MSc and, where applicable, PhD).
  • Master’s thesis or equivalent substantial research work, plus up to three other relevant scientific publications or reports.
  • A short statement (1–2 pages) explaining your experience with case-based analysis and how you would map a fraud scenario across channels, distinguish bank-visible evidence from external context, and identify legal or ethical constraints.
  • Names and contact information of at least two referees.

It is important that you both document and reflect on your competence. You are encouraged to use the NTNUs competence matrix as a guide for  documentation of your competence.

In the evaluation of which candidate is best qualified, emphasis will be placed on education, experience and personal and interpersonal qualities. Motivation, ambitions, and potential will also count in the assessment of the candidates. Open scientific practice will be recognized.

Your application will be considered by a committee at the department. Candidates of interest will be invited to an interview.

General information

Diversity is a strength, and at NTNU we aim to be an employer that reflects the diversity in society and that makes use of the potential of the population's collective skills. Our vision is Knowledge for a better world and our values ​​are creative, critical, constructive and respectful. We believe that an organization that is equal, diverse, and gender-balanced is essential for us to achieve our goals.   

We strive to attract employees with different skills, life experiences and perspectives to contribute to even better problem solving of our societal mission in research and education.  

If you think this position is relevant and interesting, we encourage you to apply, regardless of gender, functional ability, and cultural background, or whether you have been out of work for a period of time. 

At NTNU we want to increase the proportion of women in scientific positions. We have a number of measures to promote equality. 

As an employee at NTNU, you must continually maintain and improve your professional development and be flexible regarding any organizational changes.

A public list of applicants with name, age, job title and municipality of residence is prepared after the application deadline. If you want to reserve yourself from entry on the public applicant list, this must be justified. Assessment will be made in accordance with current legislation. You will be notified if the reservation is not accepted.

For the sake of transparency, candidates will be given expert evaluations of their own and other candidates. As an applicant you are considered part of the process and are stipulated by rules of confidentiality. 

If you have any questions regarding the position, please contact Prof. Raghavendra Ramachandra, email: raghavendra.ramachandra@ntnu.no . If you have questions regarding the recruitment process, please contact HR Katrine Rennan, e-mail: katrine.rennan@ntnu.no .

Application deadline: 31.12.2026.

Gjøvik is historically an industrial city linked to its location by Lake Mjøsa. Today, the region is known for high-tech companies that supply products to the automotive industry, the defense sector and international markets, among others. NTNU collaborates with many sectors, both in the private sector and public enterprises and services in information security, technology, design, logistics and health.

The city is large enough to have an active and varied cultural offer, safe local communities with kindergartens, schools and sports. It is easy to seek out nature for activities both summer and winter.

NTNU - knowledge for a better world

The Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU) creates knowledge for a better world and solutions that can change everyday life.

Research is vital to the security of our society. We teach and conduct research in cyber security, information security, communications networks and networked services. The Department of Information Security and Communication Technology is one of seven departments in the Faculty of Information Technology and Electrical Engineering .

title: Principal Pre-Commissioning Engineer
description:
Location: Lysaker, Norway (with a planned move to Kongsberg)Business Unit: EMS / Engineering (I&C)Contract Duration: 6 monthsExpected Start Date: 1 December 2026Application Deadline: 20 November 2026

About the Role

Are you an experienced Pre-Commissioning Engineer with strong expertise in subsea pipelines and umbilical systems?

We are seeking a senior engineer to provide technical expertise across subsea pre-commissioning projects, tenders, studies and offshore operations. You will focus on pipeline and umbilical testing, engineering assurance and execution planning, contributing throughout the project lifecycle.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop and review pre-commissioning philosophies, procedures and execution strategies.

  • Lead engineering activities covering FCG, hydrotesting, leak testing, flushing, dewatering, drying and preservation.

  • Define pigging strategies, including pig selection, configuration, pressure requirements and contingency plans.

  • Specify temporary equipment requirements, including pumps, filtration units, tanks, compressors and testing equipment.

  • Review pipeline and subsea designs, subcontractor procedures, methodologies and proposed equipment spreads.

  • Develop umbilical testing procedures covering electrical, fibre-optic and hydraulic systems, including continuity, insulation resistance, OTDR and pressure testing.

  • Evaluate test results and support system acceptance and handover.

  • Coordinate technical interfaces with Umbilical, SPS, Controls, Installation and offshore teams.

  • Provide engineering support during project preparation, mobilisation and offshore execution.

  • Support vessel-based operations, troubleshoot technical issues and assess operational and test data.

  • Conduct technical reviews, risk assessments and readiness assessments.

  • Provide technical assurance for assigned scopes, review critical deliverables and support the qualification of equipment and methods.

  • Contribute to tenders and studies through execution concepts, scope definition, equipment specifications, man-hour estimates and technical evaluations.

  • Provide input on vessel selection, deck requirements, schedules and offshore duration.

  • Guide and mentor engineers while contributing to procedures, technical tools, documentation and lessons learned.

Qualifications and ExperienceMust-Have Requirements

  • BSc or MSc in Mechanical, Marine, Subsea, Offshore, Petroleum Engineering or a related discipline.

  • Relevant experience in subsea and pipeline pre-commissioning engineering.

  • Strong hands-on expertise in:

    • Flooding, Cleaning and Gauging (FCG) and pigging.

    • Hydrotesting, pressure testing and subsea leak testing.

    • Pipeline dewatering and drying.

    • Electrical, fibre-optic and hydraulic umbilical testing.

  • Experience developing offshore procedures and performing engineering calculations.

  • Experience with pre-commissioning equipment spreads, including pumps, filtration systems, compressors and testing equipment.

  • Experience across project execution and tenders/FEED.

  • Good knowledge of applicable DNV requirements and industry practices.

  • Fluency in English, both written and spoken.

  • Strong technical judgement, problem-solving and communication skills.

Nice-to-Have Qualifications

  • 10+ years of relevant subsea and pipeline pre-commissioning experience.

  • Offshore and vessel-based pre-commissioning execution experience.

  • Experience providing technical guidance and mentoring to engineering teams.

  • Fluency in Norwegian, both written and spoken.

About Sperton

Sperton is a global recruitment and consulting company with offices across Europe, Asia and the Americas. We help organisations find and engage skilled professionals through flexible recruitment, consulting and global mobility solutions.

title: Senior Engineer
description:
About the position

A permanent position as Senior engineer (position code 1181) is available at The Department of Physics, University of Oslo.

Starting date as soon as possible. 

Place of work is Department of Physics at Blindern, Oslo.

Job description and work tasks

The Electronics section has seven academic positions (two full-time and five part-time) and two technical positions. The research activity is currently largely related to projects in medical technology, particularly those using methods based on impedance spectroscopy. The successful candidate may also provide technical support for new research activities in electronic components and neuromorphic electronics, especially related to electrical characterization, measurement setups, and laboratory infrastructure. 

Together with the Department of Informatics, the section is responsible for a study program in electronics, informatics, and technology. The academic staff are therefore responsible for several courses in electronics and sensor technology and also contribute to teaching basic physics courses. The section’s staff are also involved in the supervision of students at both master’s and doctoral level. 

The engineering position is intended to support both the research and teaching activities in which the section is involved. 

The tasks connected to teaching will primarily involve training and assisting master’s and PhD students in the use of specialized measuring instruments and software. 

Part of the position also involves organizing the section’s student laboratories. This includes testing of hardware and software, as well as other typical engineering tasks related to the day to-day operation of the laboratories.

What skills are important in this role?

Qualification requirements:

The minimum educational requirement is a master’s degree (or equivalent) in electronics/electrical engineering. In addition, the candidate must have experience with: 

  • Instrumentation, measurement systems, and laboratory work 
  • Impedance spectroscopy and interpretation of bioimpedance data 
  • Programming in Python and MATLAB, or equivalent 
  • Finite element modelling, e.g. COMSOL Multiphysics 
  • Good oral and written English skills

The following qualifications are strongly desirable and will be emphasized in the evaluation process: 

  • Research experience, preferably demonstrated through a PhD degree 
  • Use of various sensors for monitoring food quality, such as colorimetry, pH measurements, and NIR spectrometry 
  • Electrical characterization of semiconductor devices or other electronic components, preferably including low-current and/or pulsed measurements 
  • Automation and integration of laboratory instruments and measurement systems 
  • Technical supervision of students
What are we looking for in you?

Personal skills:

  • A service minded attitude 
  • Ability to work independently 
  • Ability to work precisely in a structured and solution-oriented manner and swiftly adapts to new tasks 
  • Good communication and collaboration skills 
  • Positive attitude and the ability to handle hectic periods 
  • Have a safety-oriented attitude

Employment in the position is based on a comprehensive assessment of all qualification requirements applicable to the position, including personal skills.

We can offer you
  • A pleasant and stimulating work environment
  • Good welfare schemes.
  • Opportunity of up to 1.5 hours a week of exercise during working hours.  A workplace with good development and career opportunities.
  • Membership in the Statens Pensjonskasse, which is one of Norway's best pension schemes with beneficial mortgages and good insurance schemes.
  • Oslo’s family-friendly surroundings with their rich opportunities for culture and outdoor activities
  • Salary in position as Senior Engineer, position code 1181 in salary range NOK 700 000 – 775 000, depending on competence and experience. From the salary, 2% is deducted in statutory contributions to the State Pension Fund
We need different perspectives in our work

UiO is an open and internationally oriented comprehensive university that strives to be an inclusive and diverse workplace and academic environment. You can read more about UiO’s work on equality, inclusion, and diversity at uio.no.

We fulfill our mission most effectively when we draw upon our variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives. We are looking for great colleagues, could you be the next one?

We will do our best to accommodate your needs. Relevant adjustments may include modifications to working hours, task adaptations, digital, technical, or physical adjustments, or other practical measures.

If you have an immigrant background, a disability, or CV gaps (Norwegian), we encourage you to indicate this in the job application portal. We always invite at least one qualified candidate from each group for an interview. In this context, disability is defined as an applicant who identifies as having a disability that requires workplace or employment-related accommodations. For more details about the requirements, please refer to the Employer portal (Norwegian).

The selections made in the job application portal are used for anonymized statistics that all state employers include in their annual reports. More information about gender equality initiatives at UiO can be found here. 

We especially encourage women to apply.We hope you will apply for the position with us.

How to apply

The application must include:

  • Cover letter with a statement of motivation
  • CV (complete overview of education and work experience)
  • Copies of educational certificates and transcript of records
  • Names and contact details of 2-3 references (names, relation to candidate and telephone number)

Your CV must be entered in Jobbnorge’s CV form and cannot be submitted only as an attachment. This requirement is intended to ensure correct documentation and record-keeping in accordance with the Public Administration Act, Section 15.

Application with attachments must be submitted via our recruitment system Jobbnorge, click "Apply for this job".

When applying for the position, we ask you to retrieve your education results from Vitnemålsportalen.no. If your education results are not available through Vitnemålsportalen, we ask you to upload copies of your transcripts or grades. Please note that all documentation must be in English or a Scandinavian language.

Formal regulations

The best qualified candidates will be invited for interviews.

Applicant lists can be published in accordance with Norwegian Freedom of Information Act § 25. When you apply for a position with us, your name will appear on the public applicant list. It is possible to request to be excluded from this list. You must justify why you want an exemption from publication and we will then decide whether we can grant your request. If we can't, you will hear from us.

Om arbeidsgiveren:

The University of Oslo is Norway’s oldest and highest rated institution of research and education with 26 500 students and 7 200 employees. Its broad range of academic disciplines and internationally esteemed research communities make UiO an important contributor to society. 

The research at the Department of Physics covers a broad range of subfields within physics and technology: From space research to medical physics. A good proportion of the research is interdisciplinary, and conducted in close cooperation with collaborators in Norway and abroad. Education and teaching are other essential activities. We offer a broad range of courses, and the Department is involved in several study programmes at bachelor’s and master’s level. Some of the best lecturers in Norway are amongst our employees, and we are proud of our prizewinning teaching and learning environment. The Department has 200 employees, of which 50 are permanent scientific positions. On a yearly basis 20 students complete their Ph.D. and 50 finish their M.Sc. degree.

title: Bli vår nye mekaniker i Ålesund – frihet, faglige utfordringer og et rått team!
description:
Er du en dyktig mekaniker som brenner for at maskiner skal fungere 100 %, yte maksimalt og se skikkelige ut? Motiveres du av varierte dager, god tillit og friheten til å legge opp din egen hverdag slik at arbeidet flyter best mulig? Da vil du trives hos oss i Cramo.

 

Hos oss blir du ikke bare en som skrur, du får det reelle ansvaret for at utleieparken i Ålesund spiller på lag. Verkstedet og maskinparken blir ditt stolte ansvarsområde, hvor du får styre prosessene, planlegge kapasiteten og ta de faglige avgjørelsene som utgjør en forskjell. Du får en nøkkelrolle med stor handlingsfrihet, samtidig som du blir en del av et uformelt og faglig sterkt team som deler erfaringer og mener at god humor er like viktig som godt håndverk.

 

Hva tilbyr vi deg?

Vi vet at en avdeling kun fungerer bra når folk trives. Derfor legger vi alt til rette for en forutsigbar og god hverdag med lavt stressnivå, selv når det koker litt ekstra.

 

  • Stor tillit og faglig eierskap: Du får styre hverdagen din i stor grad selv og ta avgjørelser som påvirker driften direkte.
  • Et sterkt fagmiljø å sparre med: Du står aldri alene! Teamet i Ålesund, sammen med erfarne mekanikere i resten av regionen, samarbeider tett og deler gladelig av sin erfaring.
  • Gode betingelser: Konkurransedyktig lønn, attraktiv bonusordning og solid pensjons- og forsikringspakke.
  • Balanse og trivsel: Vi har fokus på trivsel og at du har det bra både på og utenfor jobb. Du får støtte til trening og én betalt frivillighetsdag i året.
  • Uformell kultur: En «klart vi kan»-holdning med rom for god humor og høyt under taket.

 

Hva innebærer rollen hos oss?

Som mekaniker hos Cramo i Ålesund tar du styringen over arbeidshverdagen. Du sørger for at maskinene våre er funksjonelle, godt vedlikeholdt og fremstår visuelt flotte for kundene våre.

 

Dine viktigste oppgaver vil være:

  • Helhetlig eierskap til maskinparken: Feilsøking, service, reparasjoner og klargjøring før, under og etter utleie.
  • Styre kapasitet og innkjøp: Du vurderer arbeidsmengden fortløpende. Ved topper, servicer eller årskontroller har du mandat til å koordinere med eksterne leverandører/mekanikere.
  • Prosess- og kostnadskontroll: Du styrer hele reparasjonsløpet fra feilsøking til registrering og kostnadsføring på serviceordre, slik at drift kan fakturere reelle reparasjonskostnader videre.
  • Verksteddrift: Holde orden i delebestillinger, optimalisere verksteddriften og redusere antall maskiner som står «nede».
  • Utrykninger og feltoppdrag: Noen dager jobber du på verkstedet, andre dager drar du ut til kunden og blir helten som løser utfordringene på stedet.

 

 

Hvem ser vi etter?

Vi leter ikke etter en superhelt som kan alt fra dag en, men etter deg som brenner for mekaniker faget, liker å ha oversikt og har god teknisk forstand. Du stolt av jobben du gjør, enten du løser en kompleks feilkode eller sørger for at en maskin ser skinnende ny ut for neste kunde.

 

Det er ideelt om du har:

  • Fagbrev innen anleggs-, landbruks- eller industrimekanikk, elektro (Gr. L) eller et annet relevant mekanisk fag.
  • …men har du lang, praktisk erfaring og en "skru-hjerne" som løser det meste? Søk likevel! Hos oss veier reell kompetanse, faglig engasjement og rett innstilling veldig høyt.
  • Førerkort klasse B (har du BE eller truckførerbevis er det en fin bonus. Har du det ikke, så finner vi ut av det sammen).

  • Grunnleggende digitale ferdigheter og gode norskkunnskaper.

     

Du er en vi passe sammen med dersom du:

  • Motiveres av tillit og frihet under ansvar, og liker å ha kontroll på egne prosjekter og kostnader.
  • Trives med at det koker litt ekstra i ny og ne, men mestrer kunsten å holde hodet kaldt slik at det aldri oppleves som uoversiktlig stress.
  • Er en utpreget lagspiller som bryr seg om kollegene sine, sprer god stemning i kaffepausene og skaper en trygg, inkluderende arbeidsplass.

 

Klar for nye utfordringer?

Send oss en søknad eller ta kontakt for en uforpliktende prat om rollen! Vi gleder oss til å bli kjent med deg.

 

 

 

 

For mer informasjon eller spørsmål, kontakt oss på:

Mail: Richard.taylor@randstad.noMobil: 982 95 163

For å søke:Registrer din CV online på www.randstad.no og søk på denne stillingen.

  • Søknadsfrist - Senest 16.11.26. (Ansettelse kan bli gjort før frist)

Alle søkere vil få svar og blir kontaktet.

Om arbeidsgiveren:

Cramo er et av Norges ledende utleieselskaper innen maskiner, utstyr og modulbygg for bygg, anlegg, industri og offentlig sektor. Vi har over 30 avdelinger, mer enn 300 ansatte og er sertifisert innen kvalitet, miljø og arbeidsmiljø (ISO 9001, 14001 og 45001).

Siden 2020 har Cramo vært en del av Boels Rental, en av Europas største og mest fremtidsrettede 

aktører innen utleiebransjen. Dette gir oss et solid apparat i ryggen og gode forutsetninger for videre utvikling.

I vår avdeling jobber vi målrettet for å levere de beste løsningene i markedet, med høy aktivitet, tett samarbeid med både små og store kunder, og et fremoverlent arbeidsmiljø preget av kontinuerlig utvikling og varierte arbeidsoppgaver.

title: Vil du kombinere salg, kundekontakt og interesse for lastebilbransjen
description:
Den beste feilen er den som aldri oppstår. For kundene våre handler en lastebil om langt mer enn transport. Den skal starte hver dag, levere som planlagt og være på veien når kunden trenger den. Når service, kontroller eller nødvendige reparasjoner blir utsatt, kan det raskt føre til driftsstans og unødvendige kostnader.I Norsk Scania ønsker vi å være i forkant. Derfor ser vi nå etter en Account Manager, Rolling Fleet som vil bidra til å utvikle kundeoppfølgingen vår, identifisere nye salgsmuligheter og sørge for at kundene får mest mulig ut av kjøretøyene sine.Dette er en spennende mulighet for deg som trives med kundekontakt, motiveres av salg og liker å finne løsninger som skaper verdi for både kunden og Scania.Om rollenSom Account Manager Rolling Fleet får du en sentral rolle i oppfølgingen av våre eksisterende kunder og deres kjøretøy.Ved hjelp av kunde- og kjøretøydata skal du identifisere behov, se salgsmuligheter og tilby løsninger som bidrar til økt oppetid og en mer effektiv drift for kundene våre.Du vil ha tett dialog med kundene og samarbeide med våre verksteder, kundemottakere og salgsorganisasjonen for å sikre at behov blir fulgt opp og omgjort til konkrete salg og verkstedoppdrag.Dette er en spennende rolle for deg som vil kombinere salg, relasjonsbygging og interesse for transportbransjen.ArbeidsstedStillingen vil ha kontorsted ved et av våre Scania-anlegg på Østlandet. Vi er fleksible når det gjelder lokasjon, og endelig arbeidssted avtales i løpet av rekrutteringsprosessen.Hvem ser vi etter?Vi ser etter deg som trives med kundekontakt, er nysgjerrig på kundens behov og motiveres av å skape resultater.Vi tror du vil trives i rollen dersom du:
  • Liker å bruke telefonen som arbeidsverktøy og ta initiativ til kundedialog.
  • Har interesse for lastebiler, transportbransjen og kundens drift.
  • Er god til å bygge relasjoner og skape tillit.
  • Har et kommersielt blikk og ser muligheter for mersalg.
  • Jobber strukturert og samarbeider godt med andre.
  • Har konkurranseinstinkt og motiveres av å nå mål.
Du har gjerne erfaring fra salg, kundeservice, verksted eller transportbransjen. Relevant utdanning er positivt, men ikke avgjørende.For oss er motivasjonen din, evnen til å skape gode kunderelasjoner og viljen til å lære minst like viktig som hva som står på CV-en.Hva kan vi tilby deg?Hos Norsk Scania blir du en del av et solid, internasjonalt selskap med dyktige kolleger og et stort engasjement for både kunder og medarbeidere.Vi tilbyr deg:
  • En spennende og variert rolle med mulighet til å påvirke kundeopplevelsen og salgsresultatene.
  • Muligheten til å bidra til å utvikle vår kundeoppfølging.
  • Et godt arbeidsmiljø med engasjerte og kompetente kolleger.
  • Gode muligheter for faglig og personlig utvikling.
  • Årlige sosiale sammenkomster og aktiviteter som skaper samhold og trivsel.
  • Konkurransedyktige betingelser og gode pensjons- og forsikringsordninger.
Klar for å bli en del av Scania?Vi ser etter deg som ikke bare ser en lastebil, men også mulighetene som ligger i å holde den på veien.Hos oss får du bruke din kommersielle teft, bygge sterke kunderelasjoner og bidra til løsninger som gjør en forskjell for kundene våre.Høres dette ut som noe for deg? Da håper vi du sender oss en søknad!Har du spørsmål om stillingen, er du velkommen til å kontakte Christoffer Hermann, regionsdirektør for Region Øst Nord, på telefon 993 32 778.Søknadsfrist: Onsdag 9. desember 2026.Vi ser frem til å høre fra deg!

title: PhD Research Fellow in Experimental Proton Therapy
description:
About the position

We invite applications for a three-year PhD Research Fellow position in experimental proton therapy, available at the Department of Physics, University of Oslo (UiO).

The preferred starting date is March 1, 2027, and no later than April 1, 2027.The fellowship period is 36 months.

The position is part of InnovaRTBRAIN – Innovative Radiation Therapy for Brain Tumors, a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network (MSCA-DN) funded by the European Union. The network brings together leading European research institutions, hospitals, and industrial partners to develop innovative radiation therapy approaches for brain tumors, with particular emphasis on glioblastoma.The successful candidate will be recruited as Doctoral Candidate 13 (DC13) and will join the proton therapy research group at the Department of Physics, University of Oslo and the Department of Radiation Biology, Oslo University Hospital (OUS).

Most of the experimental research will be carried out at the proton therapy facility at Oslo University Hospital, which provides state-of-the-art infrastructure for preclinical proton irradiation, including a dedicated research beamline and gantry, a 3T small-animal MRI scanner, and facilities for experimental radiobiology.

No one can be appointed for more than one PhD Research Fellowship period at the University of Oslo. 

Background of the project

Glioblastoma is one of the most aggressive forms of brain cancer, with limited treatment options and poor prognosis. Radiation therapy plays a central role in its treatment, but its effectiveness is restricted by tumor radioresistance and the sensitivity of surrounding healthy brain tissue.

Proton minibeam radiation therapy (pMBRT) is an emerging approach in which radiation is delivered in narrow, spatially separated beams, producing a highly heterogeneous dose distribution. This technique has the potential to reduce radiation-induced damage to healthy tissues while maintaining effective tumor irradiation. However, its biological effects, particularly the evolution of tumor and normal tissue responses over time, remain incompletely understood. 

The PhD project will investigate the biological response to proton minibeam irradiation in preclinical models of brain cancer, using longitudinal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and quantitative image analysis. The project will also explore the potential of MRI-derived biomarkers for assessing treatment response and normal tissue effects. An important part of the research will be conducted in close collaboration with another doctoral candidate in InnovaRTBRAIN (DC6), based at Oslo University Hospital, who will investigate combinations of radiation therapy and immunotherapy, including CAR-T cell treatment.

Job description 

The doctoral candidate will conduct experimental studies in mouse models to investigate tumor and normal tissue responses to proton minibeam radiation therapy, using magnetic resonance imaging and other methods to characterize radiation-induced biological effects.The main responsibilities will be:

  • Plan and conduct preclinical proton minibeam irradiation experiments in mouse models
  • Acquire and analyze MRI data, including diffusion-weighted imaging, to quantify treatment response and potential normal tissue toxicity
  • Relate MR-derived image parameters to radiation dose distributions, linear energy transfer (LET), and biological endpoints
  • Develop and apply quantitative image analysis and radiomics methods to identify imaging features associated with tumor response and radiation injury
  • Investigate MRI-based biomarkers in combination with NMR-derived metabolic and relaxation-time markers, in collaboration with international project partners
  • Collaborate with DC6 on preclinical studies combining proton minibeam radiation therapy and immunotherapy
  • Participate in joint research, training activities, and research visits within the InnovaRTBRAIN doctoral network 
Research environment

The candidate will join an interdisciplinary research environment combining radiobiology, medical physics, experimental proton therapy, and medical imaging. The research will be conducted in close collaboration between the University of Oslo and Oslo University Hospital, primarily at the proton therapy research facility at the Norwegian Radium Hospital. The facility provides access to experimental proton irradiation, a dedicated small-animal MRI scanner, treatment planning software, and infrastructure for preclinical cancer research.

Supervisors and international collaboration

The doctoral candidate will be supervised by Professor Eirik Malinen (UiO/OUS), with co-supervision from Professor Nina Edin (UiO), Professor Paul Vasos (University of Bucharest), and Else Marit Inderberg (OUS). The InnovaRTBRAIN network will provide an international and interdisciplinary training environment, combining expertise in medical physics, radiobiology, imaging, cancer biology, and immunotherapy.

Planned secondments

As part of the InnovaRTBRAIN doctoral network, the candidate will undertake research visits to international academic and industrial partners:

  • University of Bucharest, Romania (3 months): Integration of NMR-based biomarkers with MRI-derived radiomics to characterize tumor responses.
  • Xstrahl, UK (2 weeks): Training in small-animal irradiation technologies and their applications in preclinical radiation therapy research.
  • COSYLAB, Slovenia (2 weeks): Exposure to industrial developments in radiation therapy technology and control systems.

These secondments will provide complementary scientific and technical training and strengthen collaboration within the InnovaRTBRAIN network.

What skills are important in this role?

The Faculty of Mathematics and Natural Sciences has a strategic ambition to be among Europe’s leading communities for research, education and innovation. Candidates for these fellowships will be selected in accordance with this, and expected to be in the upper segment of their class with respect to academic credentials. 

We are seeking a highly motivated candidate with a strong background in biophysics or physics, combined with an interest in biological and biomedical research.

Required qualifications:

  • Master’s degree or equivalent in biophysics, physics, medical physics, or a closely related field. Foreign completed degree (M.Sc.-level) corresponding to a minimum of four years in the Norwegian educational system
  • A good understanding of biological systems and processes
  • A solid foundation in quantitative methods and data analysis
  • Fluent oral and written communication skills in English 
  • Motivation for experimental biomedical research, including work with preclinical animal models
  • Willingness to participate in international research visits and training activities within the MSCA Doctoral Network 

Desired qualifications:

Knowledge or practical experience in one or more of the following areas will be considered an advantage:

  • Radiation biology
  • Proton therapy
  • Magnetic resonance imaging
  • Preclinical research, including animal models
  • Image processing or quantitative analysis of biomedical imaging data
  • Scientific programming and statistical analysis, for example using Python or MATLAB
  • Cancer biology, tumor microenvironment, or radiation-induced immune responses

Experience in all these areas is not expected. 

MSCA Doctoral Network eligibility criteria:

Applicants must also comply with the following MSCA eligibility rules:

  • Candidates must not have been awarded a doctorate previously.
  • Applicants must not have resided or carried out their main activity in the country or recruiting institution for more than 12 months in the 3 years immediately prior to the date of recruitment. See https://marie-sklodowska-curie-actions.ec.europa.eu/actions/doctoral-networks.
  • Candidates must meet the entry requirements for admission to the PhD-program of the institution to which they apply, see below for more details.
  • Applicants of any nationality are eligible. 

Language requirement:

  • Good oral and written communication skills in English
  • English requirements for applicants from outside of EU/ EEA countries and exemptions from the requirements:https://www.mn.uio.no/english/research/phd/regulations/regulations.html#toc8

Grade requirements:The norm is as follows:

  • The average grade point for courses included in the Bachelor’s degree must be C or better in the Norwegian educational system
  • The average grade point for courses included in the Master’s degree must be B or better in the Norwegian educational system
  • The Master’s thesis must have the grade B or better in the Norwegian educational system

For more information see:

The purpose of the fellowship is research training leading to the successful completion of a PhD degree. 

What are we looking for in you?

Personal skills:

We are looking for a candidate who:

  • Is motivated by experimental and interdisciplinary cancer research
  • Has strong analytical and problem-solving abilities
  • Works systematically and independently
  • Enjoys collaboration across physics, biology, and medicine
  • Has good communication skills and an interest in contributing to an international research environment

Personal suitability and motivation for the research project will be given considerable weight.

Employment in the position is based on a comprehensive assessment of all qualification requirements applicable to the position.

We can offer you
  • Exciting and meaningful tasks in an organization with an important societal mission, contributing to knowledge development, education, and enlightenment that promote sustainable, fair, and knowledge-based societal development
  • Committed colleagues in a pleasant and stimulating work environment
  • Good welfare schemes
  • Opportunity of up to 1.5 hours a week of exercise during working hours
  • A workplace with good development and career opportunities
  • Career development programmes
  • Membership in the Statens Pensjonskasse, which is one of Norway's best pension schemes with beneficial mortgages and good insurance schemes
  • Oslo’s family-friendly surroundings with their rich opportunities for culture and outdoor activities
  • Salary in position as PhD Research Fellow, position code 1017 in salary range NOK from 550 800 - 595 000, depending on competence and experience. From the salary, 2 percent is deducted in statutory contributions to the State Pension Fund 
We need different perspectives in our work

UiO is an open and internationally oriented comprehensive university that strives to be an inclusive and diverse workplace and academic environment. You can read more about UiO’s work on equality, inclusion, and diversity at uio.no.

We fulfill our mission most effectively when we draw upon our variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives. We are looking for great colleagues, could you be the next one?

We will do our best to accommodate your needs. Relevant adjustments may include modifications to working hours, task adaptations, digital, technical, or physical adjustments, or other practical measures.

If you have an immigrant background, a disability, or CV gaps (Norwegian), we encourage you to indicate this in the job application portal. We always invite at least one qualified candidate from each group for an interview. In this context, disability is defined as an applicant who identifies as having a disability that requires workplace or employment-related accommodations. For more details about the requirements, please refer to the Employer portal (Norwegian).

The selections made in the job application portal are used for anonymized statistics that all state employers include in their annual reports. More information about gender equality initiatives at UiO can be found here. We hope you will apply for the position with us.

How to apply

The application must include:

  • Cover letter - statement of motivation, research interests and suitability for the position
  • CV (summarizing education, positions, relevant research experience, technical skills and academic work - scientific publications)
  • Copies of the original Bachelor and Master’s degree diploma and transcripts of records
  • Documentation of English Language requirements. The appointed candidate cannot start in the position until approved documentation of English language proficiency has been submitted.
  • A complete list of publications and academic work that the applicant wishes to be considered by the evaluation committee
  • Names and contact details of 2-3 references (name, relation to candidate, e-mail and telephone number)

Your CV must be entered in Jobbnorge’s CV form and cannot be submitted only as an attachment. This requirement is intended to ensure correct documentation and record-keeping in accordance with the Public Administration Act, Section 15.

Application with attachments must be submitted via our recruitment system Jobbnorge, click "Apply for this job".Foreign applicants should attach an official explanation of their University's grading system.

When applying for the position, we ask you to retrieve your education results from Vitnemålsportalen.no. If your education results are not available through Vitnemålsportalen, we ask you to upload copies of your transcripts or grades. Please note that all documentation must be in English or a Scandinavian language.

Formal regulations

The best qualified candidates will be invited for interviews.Applicant lists can be published in accordance with Norwegian Freedom of Information Act § 25. When you apply for a position with us, your name will appear on the public applicant list. It is possible to request to be excluded from this list. You must justify why you want an exemption from publication and we will then decide whether we can grant your request. If we can't, you will hear from us.

Please refer to Regulations for the Act on universities and colleges chapter 3 (Norwegian), Guidelines concerning appointment to post doctoral and research posts at UiO (Norwegian) and Regulations for the degree of Philosophiae Doctor (PhD) at the University of Oslo.  

The University of Oslo has a transfer agreement with all employees that is intended to secure the rights to all research results etc.

Om arbeidsgiveren:

The University of Oslo is Norway’s oldest and highest rated institution of research and education with 26 500 students and 7 200 employees. Its broad range of academic disciplines and internationally esteemed research communities make UiO an important contributor to society. 

The research at the Department of Physics covers a broad range of subfields within physics and technology: From space research to medical physics. A good proportion of the research is interdisciplinary, and conducted in close cooperation with collaborators in Norway and abroad. 

Education and teaching are other essential activities. We offer a broad range of courses, and the Department is involved in several study programmes at bachelor’s and master’s level. Some of the best lecturers in Norway are amongst our employees, and we are proud of our prizewinning teaching and learning environment. The Department has 200 employees, of which 50 are permanent scientific positions. On a yearly basis 20 students complete their Ph.D. and 50 finish their M.Sc. degree.

title: PhD Candidate in Multimodal Sensor Data Fusion for Cultural Heritage
description:
This is NTNU

NTNU is a broad-based university with a technical-scientific profile and a focus in professional education. The university is located in three cities with headquarters in Trondheim.

At NTNU, 8,6000 employees and 44,000 students work to create knowledge for a better world.

You will find more information about working at NTNU and the application process here.   

Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_KHQjc4ndas&t=41sAbout the position

Are you interested in pursuing a doctoral degree in an international research environment? This position offers the opportunity to join the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network GLASS-CARE, collaborate with academic, museums, and industry partners across Europe, and develop expertise within a multidisciplinary research project on cultural heritage science.

As part of the GLASS-CARE network, the PhD Candidate will participate in workshops, conferences, transferable skills training, and research secondments with partner organisations. The position provides opportunities for both academic and professional development within an international setting.

The successful candidate will be offered a fixed-term, full-time position as a PhD Candidate for a period of 36 months and will be enrolled in a PhD programme leading to the award of a doctoral degree. The expected start date is 1 August 2027, and the Head of the unit will be the immediate supervisor for employment-related matters.

About the project

About the GLASS-CARE project GLASS-CARE (Green Light for Advanced Solutions in Stained-glass Conservation and Application of Research and Education) is a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network that brings together leading European universities, research institutions, and industry partners to train the next generation of heritage scientists. The project focuses on understanding, documenting, and monitoring change in cultural heritage using advanced technologies, including imaging, materials analysis, artificial intelligence, and data science. Through an interdisciplinary and international research environment, GLASS-CARE equips doctoral candidates with the skills needed to address current and future challenges in cultural heritage conservation and preservation. For more details, visit http://www.glasscare.eu/

About the DC projectWithin the GLASS-CARE project, the individual research project associated with this position (DC13) is entitled Multi-sensor data fusion for digital representation.

The PhD project will investigate computational approaches for integrating data acquired through hyperspectral imaging (HSI), multispectral imaging (MSI), X-ray fluorescence (XRF), and photoacoustic techniques.

The resulting computational framework will contribute to improved material characterization, condition assessment, and conservation decision-making for historical stained glass.The PhD candidate will address the following objectives (1) Multimodal data integration (2) Multimodal registration, alignment and data fusion (3) Feature extraction and dimensionality reduction (4) Unified digital representations (6) Validation through case studies.

Expected results: (1)  A computational framework for integrating heterogeneous imaging and analytical data into unified digital representations of stained glass. (2) Advanced data fusion methods to minimize redundancy, preserve complementary information, and reveal hidden patterns across different imaging modalities. (3) Deliver validated computational models and tools for improved material characterization, visualisation, condition assessment, and conservation decision-making. 

Duties of the position
  • Complete the doctoral education until obtaining a doctorate.
  • Carry out research of good quality within the framework described above.
  • Academic publications and popular science dissemination.
  • Participate in the Colourlab research group.
  • Participate in the network’s joint research and training activities, both online and in person pacross the GLASS-CARE partner institutions and contribute to GLASS-CARE project deliverables in accordance with the Description of Action and the project's governance procedures.
  • Participate in international activities such as conferences and/or research stays at foreign educational institutions. Particularly, secondments of a few months’ duration are foreseen to project partners in University of Antwerpen-UA Belgium, Nova University Lisbon – UNL Portugal, and Swiss National Museum-SNM Switzerland.
  • Other career-promoting work

Be prepared for changes to your work duties after employment.

Required selection criteria
  • You must have experience with image acquisition and analysis.
  • Excellent programming skills.
  • At the date of recruitment, you must NOT have been awarded a doctoral degree. Researchers who have successfully defended their doctoral thesis but have not yet formally been awarded the degree are also not eligible.
  • You must meet the requirements for admission to the faculty's Doctoral Programme in computer science, see Section 6-1 of the PhD regulations for more information.
  • You must have a relevant master's degree in computer science, electrical engineering, imaging science, conservation science or equivalent. Your degree must include a major independent project (minimum 30 ECTS) equivalent to a master’s thesis.
  • Master students can apply, but the master's degree must be obtained and documented before starting the position. 
  • You must have a strong and relevant academic background from your previous studies and have an average grade from your master’s degree study, or equivalent education, which is equal to B or better compared to NTNU's grading scale. If you do not have letter grades from previous studies, you must have an equally good academic foundation. If you have a weaker academic background, you may be considered if you can document that you are exceptionally suited for a PhD education, for example through relevant work experience and/or peer-reviewed academic works.
  • Excellent oral and written communication skills in English.
  • You must comply with the MSCA mobility rule: you must not have resided or carried out your main activity (work, studies, etc.) in the country of the recruiting organisation for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before recruitment (short stays such as holidays are not taken into account). 

The appointment is to be made in accordance with NTNUs guidelines for recruitment positions for general criteria for the position.

Preferred selection criteria
  • Knowledge of and experience with spectral imaging. 
  • Knowledge of and experience with data fusion.
  • Knowledge of and experience in conservation science will be an added advantage. 
  • Experience working in an interdisciplinary and international research environment.
  • Programming skills in Python/Matlab.
  • Excellent analytical and communication skills.
  • Ability to work in an international and interdisciplinary environment.
Personal characteristics

To complete a doctoral degree (PhD), it is important that you are able to: 

  • Have a high level of personal responsibility, initiative, motivation and ability to work in a project team as well as independently. 
  • Work in a structured way, set goals and make plans to achieve them.
  • Present and discuss your research with other professionals.
  • Get involved and contribute constructively with feedback.
  • Analyze data, assess different perspectives and draw well-founded conclusions.
  • Be flexible and open to adjusting the plan for the project as needed

Emphasis will be placed on personal qualities.

We offer

 

  • An exciting job with an important mission in society
  • Developing tasks in a strong and international professional environment
  • Career guidance and follow-up during the PhD period
  • Open and inclusive working environment with committed colleagues
  • Favorable terms as a member of the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund (SPK)
  • Free Norwegian language training at a basic level (A2)

As a PhD Candidate at NTNU, you will have access to employee benefits.

Diversity

Diversity is a strength, and at NTNU we aim to be an employer that reflects the diversity in society and that makes use of the potential of the population's collective skills. Our vision is Knowledge for a better world and our values ​​are creative, critical, constructive and respectful. We believe that an organization that is equal, diverse and gender-balanced is essential for us to achieve our goals. 

We strive to attract employees with different skills, life experiences and perspectives to contribute to even better problem solving of our societal mission in research and education. 

If you think this position is relevant and interesting, we encourage you to apply, regardless of gender, functional ability and cultural background, or whether you have been out of work for a period of time.

Salary and conditions

The position of PhD Candidate, code 1017, your gross salary will normally be NOK 580 000,- per annum depending on qualifications and seniority. This will cover the MSCA Living Allowance. In addition, mobility allowance and family allowance may be provided in accordance with MSCA regulations.

A 2% statutory contribution to the State Pension Fund is deducted from the salary.

The employment period is 3 years.

For employment as a PhD Candidate, it is a prerequisite that you gain admission to the PhD programme in Computer Science within three months of your employment contract start date, and that you participate in an organized doctoral programme throughout the period of employment.

The position is conditional on external funding.

As an employee at NTNU, it is important that you keep yourself up to date with academic and organizational changes and adapt to them.

For the necessary professional and social interaction, it is a prerequisite that you are physically present and available to the institution on a daily basis.

The successful applicant must devote full working time to the project and the doctoral training programme

The appointment is carried out in accordance with the principles of the State Employees Act, and Export control (legislation that regulates the export of knowledge, technology and services). Candidates who, after assessment of the application and attachments, are considered to bein conflict with the criteria in the latter act, will not be able to be employed.

About the application

The attachments (including a description of your scientific work) must accompany the application as these documents form the basis of the application assessment. The documents must be in Norwegian/a Scandinavian language or English.

Please note: the application will only be assessed on the basis of the information we have received by the application deadline. Therefore, make sure that your application clearly shows how your skills and experience meet the criteria described above. The application and all attachments must be sent electronically via Jobbnorge.no. If you are invited to an interview, you must bring certified copies of certificates and diplomas upon request.

The application must include: 

  • Transcripts and diplomas for Bachelor's and Master's degrees.
  • CV.
  • Copy of master’s thesis. If you have recently submitted your master’s thesis, you can attach a draft of the thesis. Documentation of  completed master’s degree must be presented before taking up the position. Those who are currently doing their master thesis, submit the summary (3-4 pages).
  • Project outline containing proposals for an overall description of research questions, theoretical perspectives, methodological design for the project and progress plan (maximum 1600 words/4 pages).
  • Short letter of motivation (400 words/1 page).
  • Scientific publications or other documentation of previous research work.
  • Names and contact information of three relevant referees.
  • Completed GLASS-CARE questionnaire (available at Glass-Care website).

If all, or parts, of your education has been taken abroad, we also ask you to attach documentation of the scope and quality of your entire education, both Bachelor's and Master's education, in addition to other higher education. If your institution uses “diploma supplement” (normal for most European institutions), you must attach this. A description of the documentation required can also be found here. If you already have a statement from Norwegian Directorate for Higher Education and Skills (HK-dir), please attach this as well.

Joint work will be considered. If it is difficult to identify your contribution to joint work, you must attach a brief description of your participation.

When assessing the best qualified, we emphasize necessary qualifications such as education, experience and personal suitability. Motivation for the position, ambitions, and potential for research will also count when assessing the candidates.NTNU recognizes a wide range of academic contributions and has committed itself to The San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment and CoARA (responsible assessment of research and recognition of a greater breadth of academic contributions in accordance with NTNU's social mission).

Evaluation processApplications will be assessed by an expert committee based on the qualifications and documentation submitted by the applicants. The evaluation will consider academic achievements, the quality and relevance of the applicant's educational background, research potential, and suitability for the position. Shortlisted candidates may be invited for an interview. The final appointment will be made in accordance with the applicable regulations for employment at the university.

General information

A public list of applicants with name, age, job title and municipality of residence is prepared after the application deadline. If you wish to be exempt from entry on the public applicant list, this must be justified. Assessment will be made in accordance with current legislation. You will be notified if the exemption is not granted.

If you think this position looks interesting and in line with your qualifications, you are welcome to apply.

If you have any questions about the position, please contact Professor Sony George, +47 92556485, email sony.george@ntnu.no. 

If you have any questions about the recruitment process, please contact HR at the department: hr@idi.ntnu.no.

Application deadline: 31.01.2027

For practical information about working at NTNU, please visit this webpage.
